overview.headline: From relative rock layers to absolute radiometric dates revealing deep time

keyPoints.point: Earth is 4.54 billion years old and deep time remains hard to grasp
keyPoints.quote: Earth is 4.54 billion years old, a span of time that is hard for many people to grasp.

keyPoints.point: Steno superposition principle places older rocks at bottom and younger rocks on top
keyPoints.quote: The law of superposition says that older rocks are on the bottom and younger rocks are on the top.

keyPoints.point: Hutton proposed uniformitarianism as foundational principle of geology in 1788
keyPoints.quote: In 1788, James Hutton proposed what would become the foundational principle of geology — uniformitarianism.

keyPoints.point: Smith faunal succession law states species become extinct and replaced by new species
keyPoints.quote: Smith developed the law of faunal succession, which states that species become extinct and are replaced by new species

keyPoints.point: half-life is length of time for parent isotopes to decay to stable daughter isotope
keyPoints.quote: A half-life is the length of time it takes for half of the number of original, or parent, isotopes to decay to a stable daughter isotope.

keyTerms.gloss: branch of geology that studies rock layers to order geologic events
keyTerms.quote: principles of stratigraphy — or the branch of geology concerned with the study of rock layers

keyTerms.gloss: principle that processes shaping Earth today also shaped Earth in the past
keyTerms.quote: In 1788, James Hutton proposed what would become the foundational principle of geology — uniformitarianism.

keyTerms.gloss: law that older rocks lie below younger rocks indicating relative age
keyTerms.quote: The law of superposition says that older rocks are on the bottom and younger rocks are on the top.

keyTerms.gloss: law that species assemblages appear in same order everywhere and mark age
keyTerms.quote: Smith developed the law of faunal succession, which states that species become extinct and are replaced by new species

keyTerms.gloss: time for half of parent isotopes to decay to stable daughter isotope
keyTerms.quote: A half-life is the length of time it takes for half of the number of original, or parent, isotopes to decay to a stable daughter isotope.

keyTerms.gloss: gaps in geologic record that represent missing time between rock layers
keyTerms.quote: He also understood the concept of unconformities (gaps in the geologic record that represent missing time)
